title: Explore geographic variation
text: Strawberry Poison Dart Frog (Oophaga pumilio) exhibits remarkable geographic variation coloration across range Central America (Wang Shaffer 2008). Populations display striking differences dorsal ventral coloration, ranging bright red blue legs green, yellow, even white morphs. system provides excellent opportunity demonstrate map_locations() can used explore spatial patterns phenotypic variation using image records. First, query image records species iNaturalist: raw query returns available image records, including fall outside species’ natural range (e.g., observations zoos, captive specimens, misidentified individuals regions). focus analysis wild populations within native distribution, restrict dataset records Central America. Additionally, keep map manageable vignette avoid overcrowding, sample observations evenly across geographic range splitting latitudinal range 50 bins selecting one record per bin. Note observations multiple associated images, sample level observation keys: users click observation circle, popup window appears displaying image(s) associated record along relevant metadata. functionality allows researchers visually inspect color morph present locality, enabling rapid assessment geographic patterns coloration. observations contain multiple images (e.g., different angles life stages), users can navigate using arrow buttons bottom popup. default metadata includes observation key, contains link original record repository, can used explore additional information record. Users can download image simply clicking .
code: # get metadata op_image <- query_inaturalist(   species = "Oophaga pumilio",   format = "image" ) # restrict only to those in its natural range (Central America) op_image_ca <- op_image[   op_image$latitude >= 7 &     op_image$latitude <= 15 &     op_image$longitude >= -90 &     op_image$longitude <= -80 &     !is.na(op_image$latitude), ]  # sample homogeneously across the geographic range # split latitude in 50 bins op_image_ca$latitude_bins <- cut(   op_image_ca$latitude,   breaks = seq(7, 15, length.out = 50) )  # sampled keys sampled_keys <- op_image_ca$key[!duplicated(op_image_ca$latitude_bins)] set.seed(123) op_image_ca_sample <- op_image_ca[op_image_ca$key %in% sampled_keys, ]  # make map map_locations(   metadata = op_image_ca_sample )
